chunks: God has not sanctioned Baheerah or Sa'ibah, Waseelah or Ham. The unbelievers fabricate lies of God, for many of them are devoid of sense.

key_terms.بَحِيرَةٍ: A camel whose ears were slit, dedicated to idols or God, and not ridden or used for work.
key_terms.حَامٍ: A male camel whose offspring were dedicated to idols, connected to a specific female ancestor.
key_terms.سَائِبَةٍ: An animal set free to graze without a shepherd, dedicated to idols.
key_terms.لَا يَعْقِلُونَ: They do not use their intellect/reason.
key_terms.وَصِيلَةٍ: A female camel whose offspring were dedicated to idols, connected to a specific male ancestor.

ai.seo_question: What are Baheerah, Sa'ibah, Waseelah, and Ham in Islamic theology?
ai.summary: This verse critiques the pre-Islamic Arab customs of *bahirah*, *sa'ibah*, *wasilah*, and *ham*—where livestock were designated for idols or specific families—by affirming they were human inventions rather than divine decrees. In Shia exegesis, this highlights the *fasad* (corruption) of the disbelievers who attributed these arbitrary rituals to God due to a lack of rational understanding (*la ya'qilun*). It serves as a foundational argument against *bid'ah* (innovation) in worship, emphasizing that true divine command is based on reason and revelation, not cultural fabrication.
